questions.q: SpeedyBee F405 V4: motors M3 and M4 sit on TIM3 CH3/CH4 and run DSHOT600 through the timer and DMA. Why can a servo not be put on a free channel of the same TIM3?
options: TIM3 has no free DMA stream left: both streams are taken by the DShot of motors M3 and M4, and a servo needs its own
The period and prescaler are shared by the timer: DShot600 needs PSC 6/ARR 19, a 50 Hz servo — PSC 83/ARR 19999
Betaflight forbids `resource SERVO` on pins of a timer where a motor is already assigned and gives an error on save
The TIM3 channels output 3.3 V logic, and a servo on this timer needs a 5 V signal through a level shifter
questions.explain: A channel sets only the width (CCR); the time base is shared by the timer. timerAllocate() does not block a neighboring channel, and servoDevInit() runs after the motors and will overwrite the base — DShot on M3/M4 will break. A servo does not need DMA.

questions.q: In the CLI `resource SERVO 1 NONE` and `resource SERVO 2 B10` were typed, `feature CHANNEL_FORWARDING` was enabled, and it was saved. What will be on pad B10?
options: AUX1: forwarding starts from the first servo created, and that will be SERVO 2 on pad B10
AUX2: the resource number SERVO 2 corresponds to the second AUX channel with channel_forwarding_start = 4
Nothing: servoDevInit() stops at the first empty SERVO, and no servo is created
A constant 1500 µs from servo_center_pulse, because SERVO 1 is not assigned and forwarding shifts
questions.explain: The loop in servoDevInit() breaks at the first empty ioTag. Servos are assigned in order, starting from SERVO 1.

questions.q: A QUADX quad with SERVO_TILT enabled. The pilot added `smix 0 0 5 100 0 0 100 0` so that the gimbal tilt follows the pitch stick. What will change?
options: The tilt will follow the pitch stick at 100 % on top of CAMSTAB stabilization, in any flight mode and while disarmed
The tilt will follow the pitch stick, but only while the CAMSTAB mode is on from the switch
The CLI will reject the rule: source 5 (RC pitch) is not allowed for gimbal servo 0 in the QUADX mixer
Nothing: on QUADX servoMixer() is not called, and smix rules are loaded only for CUSTOMAIRPLANE/CUSTOMTRI
questions.explain: servoTable() calls servoMixer() only for airplane and similar mixers, and loadCustomServoMixer() — only for CUSTOMAIRPLANE and CUSTOMTRI. A gimbal on a quad is computed by the SERVO_TILT formula.

questions.q: SERVO_TILT, CAMSTAB is on, `gimbal_mode = NORMAL`, `servo 0 1000 2000 1500 50 -1`. The frame is tilted in pitch by +12°. What is the pulse of the pitch servo?
questions.explain: servoTable(): middle + rate·pitch_decideg/50 = 1500 + 50·120/50 = 1620 µs, that is, rate/5 = 10 µs per degree.

questions.q: A quad with SERVO_TILT and CHANNEL_FORWARDING enabled, `channel_forwarding_start = 4`. Which output will AUX1 go to?
options: SERVO 1, forwarding always starts from the first output
SERVO 2, right after the pitch servo
SERVO 3: the first two outputs are taken by the gimbal servos
Nowhere: the SERVO_TILT and CHANNEL_FORWARDING features are incompatible
questions.explain: writeServos() first writes servo[0] and servo[1] of the gimbal, then forwardAuxChannelsToServos(servoIndex) from index 2, that is, SERVO 3.

questions.q: 2025.12 firmware was built in Betaflight App through Cloud Build for an F405, and the CLI has no `servo` and `smix` commands. Why?
options: USE_SERVOS is in the common_pre.h block for non-cloud builds only; a cloud build needs the SERVOS option
In 2025.12 the servo and smix commands were moved to the Servos tab of the application and removed from the CLI entirely
Servos in Betaflight 2025.12 are supported only on F7/H7; an F405 does not have enough timers for servos
feature SERVO_TILT has to be enabled first, followed by a reboot; the commands appear only after save
questions.explain: The `#if !defined(CLOUD_BUILD) && !defined(SITL)` block in target/common_pre.h defines USE_SERVOS. Cloud Build gets it only with the SERVOS option or, from 2025.12, through the WING package (in 4.5 — only SERVOS).

questions.q: A pilot connected two MG996R servos (2.5 A at stall at 6 V per the datasheet) to the flight controller's five volts. What will most likely happen, and what is the right way?
options: Nothing serious: servos draw current only when moving, on average a few hundred milliamps for both
The servos will get slower; raise servo_pwm_rate to 333 Hz so that they get pulses more often
The flight controller's signal pad will overheat; put a 1 kΩ resistor in series with the signal wire
A 5 V sag and a flight controller reset at stall; power them from a separate BEC with a common ground
questions.explain: Two servos at stall — about 5 A, and the flight controller's BEC already feeds the receiver and peripherals. The servo positive supply — from a separate BEC, a common ground, and only the signal from the flight controller.

questions.q: An airplane mixer, an `smix` rule with speed 10, a PID loop of 8 kHz. How long will the rule output take to go from 0 to 500 (1500 → 2000 µs)?
options: 6.25 ms: speed is a step per PID loop, 50 loops of 125 µs
0.5 s: speed is a step per 10 ms
50 ms: speed is counted per loop at 1 kHz
Instantly: speed affects only RC sources
questions.explain: servoMixer() is called in subTaskMotorUpdate every PID loop; 500/10 = 50 loops × 125 µs = 6.25 ms. The “1 ms per loop” description in the documentation is out of date.
